key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings improve long-term corrosion resistance, while higher humidity reduces coating friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray process control can help protect carbon-steel components, with service humidity influencing tribological performance.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Characterize droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and sliding wear under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links greater porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate with increasing humidity.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance values or humidity ranges, limiting quantitative guidance for process selection and service conditions.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
